name: Returns and exchanges
description: A return is a kind of ticket, not a second inbox: the customer asks from their order, the conversation happens in the enquiry, and the money, the stock and the order status move through the shop's own code. An exchange is a new order linked to the old one.

settings.label: Offer a return in these order statuses
settings.help: The shop's own statuses, ticked by the shop — nobody else knows which of them means "the customer has it". Tick none and the button is never offered.

settings.label: Only for orders we recorded as paid
settings.help: Off by default on purpose: plenty of shops watch payment in their CRM or their accounting system rather than here, and there this check would refuse a perfectly lawful return.

settings.label: Within, days of the order
settings.help: Empty means no limit. Counted from when the order was placed.

settings.label: Put received goods back into stock by default
settings.help: Which way the radio is set when the receipt form opens — not a rule. What actually happens to a parcel is decided when it is opened: a warranty item goes back to the manufacturer or into the bin, and adding it to stock would put a broken thing on sale.

settings.label: When a return is completed, move the order to
settings.help: Applied only when nothing is left of the order to return — half an order coming back does not make the order returned. Statuses that put stock back are not offered: this module has already returned the lines, and such a status would count the same goods twice.
